propositions: A model class configured with provider='bedrock' and a canonical versioned Bedrock model id (containing ':' in the version suffix) has its explicit provider silently discarded by _resolve_target's colon-presence test

The function _resolve_target returns an unqualified model string when it contains ':' anywhere, treating version colons as provider separators, causing downstream infer_provider to misinterpret the model id fragment as a provider name
Two independent colon-scan implementations (_resolve_target and infer_provider) can drift apart and fail identically; they must route through a single shared qualifier-parsing function
An explicitly configured provider must be checked and honored before the model string is scanned for inline qualifiers, preventing punctuation in model ids from voiding configured settings
A conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pair must raise an error rather than silently picking one, since either choice discards an explicit instruction
